name: Eve
subtitle: where Christmas is always tomorrow
story: On Eve, Christmas is always tomorrow. It has been tomorrow for nine hundred years. The stockings are up, the snow is down, and the children are far too excited to sleep, which is a problem, because they haven't slept since they were born. Nobody has ever needed to buy a present: why would you, with a whole day to go? Then, one morning, the sign in the square changed.
hook: A planet for every last-minute Christmas shopper.

episode.opener: On Eve, Christmas is always tomorrow.

beats.text:
It has been tomorrow
for nine hundred years.

The stockings are up.
The snow is down.

The children are too excited
to sleep, and always have been.

Every night, the whole planet
goes to bed early, so it'll come quicker.

Nobody has ever bought a present.
There's a whole day to go.

Then, one morning,
the sign changed.

episode.caption:
Read the sign by the trees.

Eve: 2.4 million people, a 25-hour day, one moon, and Christmas, which has been tomorrow for nine hundred years. The stockings are up. The snow is down. The children are far too excited to sleep, and have been since birth. Every evening the whole planet goes to bed early so it'll come quicker. Nobody has ever bought a present, because why would you, with a whole day to go?

I brought one for my host. She cried, and then she panicked.

(The story goes that Christmas Eve is part of Christmas because the old church day began at sunset, so the feast started the evening before. On Eve, it never got past the evening.)

What would you buy with one morning's notice?

first_comment: Boxing Day is now expected in about nine hundred years.

short.title:
Christmas here
is always tomorrow.

beats.text:
No need to shop yet.
It's not till tomorrow.

The morning after you land,
the sign changes.

short.end_kicker: For everyone who shops on Christmas Eve.
